translations.text: Lo! I sat alone within a grove, sheltered by a covering, in the middle of a wood, where the streams sounded and ran in the midst of an enclosure, just as I say.

Pleasant plants also grew and blossomed there amid that throng in a peerless field, and the forest trees swayed and sounded through the terror of the winds; the sky was stirred up, and my wretched mind was all troubled.
Then suddenly, afraid and sad, I began these grim verses in song, just as you said; I remembered my sins, the wrongs of my life, and the long time, and the dark coming of death on earth.

I also dread the great judgment for my wicked deeds on earth, and I also dread the eternal anger from God himself against me and every sinful one, and how the mighty Lord will divide and judge all mankind through his secret power.
I also remembered the glory of the Lord and of the saints in the kingdom of heaven, and likewise the evils and torments of the wretched.
I remembered this within myself, and I mourned greatly, and, troubled in mind, I spoke lamenting: "Now I ask you all, my veins, that you open your springs well, hot upon my cheeks,
quick to tears, when I, sinful, strike hard with my fist, beat my breast in the place of prayer, and lay my body on the earth, and call upon all the pains I have deserved.
I ask you now with prayers that you hold back not at all from tears, but afflict my sorrowful cheeks with weeping and soon pour salt drops over them, and lay open my wickedness to the eternal Lord.

Let nothing at all of base sins remain within, in the recess of the heart, that is not made known as plain as day; let what was hidden be all laid bare in open words, of breast and of tongue and of flesh likewise.

This is the one healing for a wretched soul and the best of hopes for the sorrowing: that he here make known his wounds with weeping to the heavenly physician, who alone can heal the mind that has slipped with good, and quickly unbind captives;
nor will the ruler of angels crush the heedless mind with his right hand, nor will Christ the Ruler quench with water the lukewarm smoke of feeble flax.
Has not the thief who was put to death with Christ on the cross set you a sharp example of how much true repentance for sins and guilt avails, and how glorious it is?
The thief on the cross was guilty and wicked, all laden with misdeeds; nevertheless, close to death, he offered his prayers to the Lord with the thoughts of his heart.
With few but faithful words he quickly obtained his salvation and help, and went in through the peerless gates of paradise with the Saviour.
I ask you, O wretched mind, why do you delay so long in making yourself known to the physician, or why are you silent, [?]
Sinful tongue, now that you have a time ready for forgiveness, now that the Almighty, guardian of the kingdom of heaven, gladly hears you with attentive ears?
But the day will come when God will judge the whole circuit of the earth; you alone must give account in words before God the Creator, and render what is due to the mighty Lord.
I counsel you to be quicker with penitent tears, and to forestall the anger of the eternal Judge.
Why do you lie in filth, flesh, filled with vices and sins? Why do you not cleanse your grievous sins with a flood of tears?
Why do you not ask the Lord of life for poultices and plaster, the medicines of life?
Now you must weep and shed tears while there is time and a season for weeping. Now it is healing for a person to weep here and do penance to please the Lord.
The Son of God will be glad if you suffer sorrow and judge yourself for your sins on earth; and the God of heaven will not punish injuries and sins more than once for any man.
You must not despise lamentation and weeping and the time that is ready for forgiveness.

Remember also in your mind how great the punishment is that the wretched will suffer for their former deeds, or how terribly and how awesomely the King of high majesty will judge each and every one here according to their former deeds,
[?] or what portents begin to come and make known Christ's coming on earth.
All the earth trembles; likewise the hills crumble and fall, the slopes of the mountains bend and melt, and the terrible roar of the stormy sea greatly troubles the minds of all men.
The heaven above will also be all black and darkened, heavily overcast, dark and dim of hue, and the chaos will be black.
Then the stars will fall from their places, and the sun will grow dark at once in the morning, and the moon will have no power at all to drive off [?] the darkness of the night.
Then too signs that foretell death will come here from heaven above and terrify the wretched.
when the heavenly troops come, a mighty host stirred up, and the whole army of angels throngs around and surrounds the Eternal One, the glorious Creator, with might and majesty.
Then the sun-bright Lord of the heavens will sit on his high throne, honoured with a helmet.
We will suddenly be brought before him, having come from everywhere into his presence, so that each one may receive judgement for his deeds from the Lord himself.

I ask you, man, to remember how great the terror will be then before the Lord's judgement seat. The greatest of hosts will stand there without heart and cowardly, bewildered and confounded, powerless and afraid.
Then the whole host of angels will come together from the shelter of heaven and surround the Eternal One.

Then there will be a great summons, and the whole race of Adam among the earth-dwellers will be called there: everyone who was ever fed on earth, or whom a mother bore as a human being, or those who were, or would be, or were counted in any way as yet to come.

Then on that day the secret thoughts of all will be revealed to all: everything harmful that the heart thought, or that the tongue cried out to cause injury, or that a man's hand did of wickedness in dark hiding places on earth.
All the sins in the world that anyone was ashamed to reveal or make known to any man will then be open to all together, and what someone long concealed will be equally laid open [?].
On top of all this, the whole upper air will also be filled with poisonous flame.

Fire will travel over everything. There will be no obstacle there, and no one will be able to resist its might. Everything under the course of the sky that seems to us empty, as far as the eye can see, will all at once be filled with red flame.
Then the fiery flame will blow and crackle, red and fierce. It will rush and hurry to bring torment on the sinful.
The avenging fire will not turn aside or show mercy to anyone there, unless he has been cleansed of his filth here and comes there thoroughly purified.
Then many nations, a countless number of peoples, will beat their sinful breasts hard with their fists, afraid because of their sinful desires.
Paupers and kings of peoples will be there, poor and rich, and all will be afraid. There the poor man and the wealthy man will have one law, because all of them will be afraid together.
That cruel flood will rush with fire and burn the wretched souls bitterly, and swift worms will cut and tear the hearts of those guilty of sin.

No one there can be confident in his own deserts when near the Judge. Instead terror will run through everyone together, through the thoughts of the heart, and bitter weeping too, and there the whole wicked crowd will stand stiffened, most like stone, expecting evil.
What are you doing, O flesh? What are you enduring now?
What can you do at that time but weep over your need?
Woe to you now, you who serve this world, live happily here in wantonness, and stir yourself on with the hard goads of lust!
Why do you not fear the terror of the fire, and dread for yourself the fierce torments that the Lord long ago appointed for the devils, the accursed spirits, as a reward of woes?
These things will overwhelm the mind and speech of every person by their greatness.
No speech could recount in stories to anyone on earth the wretched torments, the places full of fire in the depths, that are [?] in grim torment in hell.
There, to cause sorrow, the smoky flame and the fierce ice are mingled together, very hot and very cold, in the midst of hell.
Sometimes eyes there weep beyond measure because of the burning of the furnace (it is all full of evil); and sometimes men's teeth there gnash because of the great cold.
Wretched men will go through this dire alternation in there for ever and ever, between darkened black nights and the misery and smoke of boiling pitch.
There no voice sounds except harsh weeping and wailing, nothing else. Nor is the face of any creature seen there, except those of the tormentors who torment the wretched.
Nothing will be found in there except flame and cold and loathsome foulness. With their noses they can smell nothing but an immense stench.
There the wailing lips are filled with spewed flames, with the burning of hateful fire, and savage worms tear at them and gnaw their bones with burning teeth.

On top of all this, the wretched breast will be terrified and afflicted with bitter care over why the sinful flesh, in that perilous time, committed so many sins against itself that it should be tormented in prison, where the terrible eternal punishments are.
There no little spark of light shines for the wretched, and neither mercy nor peace nor hope nor quiet gladdens the crowd of those who weep in any way.
Comfort flees away. There is no help there that can give protection against those bitter things.
No face of any joy is found there. Instead there is terrible dread and fear and a sorrowful mind, fierce gnashing of teeth.
There cruel sorrow will be everywhere, and sickness, anger and sloth. And there sinful souls also burn and run about in flame in a dark pit.

Then the harmful joys of this world dwindle away from here and depart altogether. Then drunkenness dwindles away along with feasting, laughter and play leap off together, and lust also departs from here.
Greed departs far off, vice goes away, and every guilty wantonness then hastens into the shadow. Wretched, idle sleep, slack with slumber, flees and slinks off behind.

Then at the end the wretched one, blinded [?] in bitter flames, will look on what is now unlawful. What was dearest in life will then be hateful, and the weary mind will turn over its sins intensely, with sorrows and with lamentation.

Oh, blessed and more than blessed, the most blessed of all beings for ever and ever, is the one who in prosperity can well avoid such torments and punishments, and who likewise gladly thrives for his lord in the world in everything, and may then have the kingdom of heaven. That is the greatest of hopes.
There night never takes away the radiance of the heavenly light with darkness. No sorrow or pain or wearied old age comes there, and no toil ever happens there,
nor hunger, nor thirst, nor wretched sleep. There is no fever there, no sickness, no sudden death, no crackling of flame, and no hateful cold.
There is no sadness or sloth there, no ruin or care or fierce torment. There is no lightning or hateful storm, no winter or thunder or anything cold, and no hard hailstorms with snow.

There is no poverty or loss there, no terror of death, no misery, no anguish [?], and no mourning of any kind. Instead, peace reigns there together with prosperity, and mercy and eternal good, glory and honour, and likewise praise and life and lovely harmony.
Beyond all this, the eternal Lord gladly provides them with every good thing, where, ever present, he honours them all. The Father together receives and blesses them,
glorifies them and keeps them well, adorns them beautifully, loves them freely, and honours [?] them on the high heavenly throne.
His joyful Son, the giver of victory, gives to each one an eternal reward, heavenly ornaments, which is a noble gift, among the peerless host of angels and the troops and throngs of the saints.

There they will be joined in fellowship among the patriarchs and holy prophets with rejoicing minds, in the midst of the cities [?], where the messengers of Almighty God are, and among the red companies of roses, where they will always shine.

There the company of white-clad virgins moves about, hung with blossoms, the brightest of hosts. They are all led by God's peerless beloved, the lady who bore us the Lord, the Creator on earth: the pure maiden.

That is Mary, best of maidens. She, most blessed of all, leads [?] through the beautiful shining kingdoms of the glorious Father, between Father and Son, with a noble company, and among the counsellors of the kingdom of eternal heavenly peace, the guardians of the heavens.

What can be hard here in this life, if you will tell the truth to whoever asks, compared with being allowed to live fearless among that company for eternity, and to enjoy bliss without end from then on in the blessed seats of the heavenly ones?"
